function: A named set of steps in the code. Other code 'calls' it by name to get that job done, like asking a coworker for help.
call: When one piece of code runs a function. On the map, a wire from the caller to the function it asks.
file: One text file of code. On the map, a box you can open to see the functions inside it.
import: A line at the top of a file that borrows code from another file or a library.
library: Code written by someone else that this project borrows, such as a date or web framework.
parameter: An input a function needs to do its job, given in the brackets when it is called.
return value: What a function hands back when it finishes.
class: A blueprint that groups data and the functions that work on it, like a recipe for making many similar things.
variable: A named box that holds a value, such as a number or some text, so the code can use it later.
loop: Code that repeats the same steps for each item in a list.
condition: An if/else check: do one thing when something is true, another when it is not.
build: Turning source code into the finished files that run or get published.
API: A way for one program to ask another for something, often over the internet.
component: A reusable piece of a user interface, like a button or a card, written once and used in many places.
config: A settings file. The code reads it instead of having the values written into the code.
test: Code that checks other code gives the right answers, so mistakes are caught early.
database: Where an app keeps its data so it is still there next time.
server: A program that waits for requests (from a browser or an app) and answers them.
